body.statement: For every heavy arm, choose \(J_n\) and the derived \(M_n\) from \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\). Then the deterministic and centered Knight remainders of \(\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}\) converge uniformly on compact local-parameter sets to \(f_a(\tau)t^2/2\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\theta_a=\vartheta_a\), the preliminary quantiles and every wholly empirical drift component are consistent, and \[\left(\frac{n}{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.\] By \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\), the endpoint mark step requires only total-variation convergence of the finite score vector \(\Psi_a(Y(a))\) to \(H_a\); no convergence of the full conditional outcome law is required. The true-propensity fixed-quantile law is recovered by replacing the fitted propensity and empirical clip by their population counterparts.
body.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem, with its transfer condition proved from primitives.
body.gap: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky prove the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile law and no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.
body.consumer: Observational QTE analyses can use flexible assignment models while retaining full-population non-Gaussian calibration.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish uniform consistency of every wholly empirical centering component after the feasible-to-oracle score and curvature transfer.
obligation.obstruction: The current primitives do not control the fitted Hill statistic at the intermediate order, the nested preliminary quantiles, the random endpoint-score denominator, or the weighted kernel density uniformly over the class.
obligation.attempted: Proved the corrected score-transfer inequality from the amplified tail error and the interior discrepancy, and reduced the Knight curvature to the stated density modulus and relative-square bound.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)\) and \(S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)\) denote the feasible and population-weight linear Knight scores, both divided by \(h_{a,n}\).  On \(\{\pi_a\le u_{a,n}\}\), the reciprocal identity
\[
\frac1{\widehat\pi\vee b}-\frac1{\pi\vee b}
=-\frac{\widehat\pi-\pi}
{(\widehat\pi\vee b)(\pi\vee b)}
\]
and the punctured relative bound imply
\[
|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}|
\le C E_{a,n}\,h_{a,n}^{-1}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le u_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
+|D_{a,n}|+o_P(1).
\]
Hall integration gives
\[
E\!\left[
h_{a,n}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le u_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
\right]
=O(M_n^{\gamma_a-1}),
\]
and its centered part has no larger order after truncation.  Hence
\[
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
|S^{\rm fe}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\rm or}_{a,n}(\tau)|
=O_P\{E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1)
=o_P(1).
\]
The conditional-density modulus similarly turns Knight's integral remainder into
\[
\frac12f_a(\tau)t^2+o_P(1)
\]
uniformly for bounded \(t\), once the relative-weight square integral is available.  Thus the score-transfer and curvature portions reduce rigorously to the narrowed boundary-likelihood lemma.  Still missing are uniform consistency proofs for the generalized-inverse scale, the nested preliminary quantiles, the fitted-tail Hill statistic, the endpoint-score ratio, and the weighted density estimate.  None of those conclusions is implied merely by the three likelihood bounds, so the full theorem remains open.
